Build the app described below in an existing Next.js 16 project (App Router, React 19, strict TypeScript).

Stack: Once UI (`@once-ui-system/core` 2.1) is installed and its standard providers are mounted in the root layout; its agent documentation is in the `docs/` folder, which you can read (start with `docs/AGENTS.md`).

Task: Lumen's onboarding at `/`: a four-step wizard (1 Account: name and work email; 2 Workspace: workspace name and team size; 3 Invite: up to three teammate emails, skippable; 4 Preferences: theme and weekly digest). A step indicator shows where the user is. Back and Next move between steps; Next validates the current step and shows inline errors instead of moving on. A summary card beside the form (below it on phones) shows what has been entered so far. Finishing goes to `/welcome`, a done screen with a short checklist of next steps.

Use this data for the content (define it in the code; you may put it in `lib/data.ts`):

```json
{
  "product": "Lumen, a product-analytics and issue-tracking app for small software teams",
  "user": {
    "name": "Maya Okafor",
    "email": "maya@acmelabs.io",
    "role": "Owner"
  }
}
```

Requirements:
- The app must serve these routes: `/`, `/welcome`. Each route default-exports its page from its `page.tsx`; nested layouts are allowed.
- Write as many files as the app needs, under `app/`, `components/` or `lib/`. Do not change any file that already exists in the project except `app/page.tsx`. The root layout, global styles and the stack's standard providers already exist. You can read the project's existing files under `project/`.
- Put "use client" at the top of every file that uses state, effects or event handlers.
- Use realistic placeholder content defined in the files (no lorem ipsum). Load nothing from the network: no external image, font or API URLs.
- The app must type-check under strict TypeScript, pass `next build`, and render every route without console errors.
- Make it responsive from phone to desktop, and accessible.
- Reply with every file, each in its own fenced code block whose opening line names the file's path, like ```tsx app/settings/page.tsx, and nothing else.

# @once-ui-system/core — agent harness

This package ships an agent-first codegen harness under `ai/`, next to this file. Use it when **writing Once UI code**, not full MDX documentation pages. Paths below are relative to this file (in an app: `node_modules/@once-ui-system/core/`).

## Starting an app

A new signed-in app (sidebar, top bar, content panel) starts from `ai/starters/app/`: a working Next.js App Router setup with Once UI's CSS, fonts, providers and theme in `src/app/layout.tsx`, the shell mounted once in `src/app/(app)/layout.tsx`, and two pages. Copy it over the create-next-app files, then edit it rather than rewriting it:

```bash
cp -r node_modules/@once-ui-system/core/ai/starters/app/src/. src/ && rm -f src/app/page.module.css src/app/globals.css
```

No `src/` folder? Copy into the project root instead.

Can't run shell commands (you can only read files and reply with code)? Then nothing was copied, and an import of `AppShell` or `resources/app` breaks the build. Write the starter files your code imports (`components/AppShell.tsx`, `resources/app.ts`) in your reply, taking their content from `ai/starters/app/src/`, keep the project's own `app/layout.tsx`, and import only files you write or have opened in the project.

The copy takes `src/` only: also set `experimental.optimizePackageImports: ["@once-ui-system/core"]` in `next.config`, as `ai/starters/app/next.config.ts` does, or every route that imports the package root from a server component ships about 110 kB of extra JavaScript. That setting only works with webpack. Under Turbopack (the default for `next build` in Next 16), a server component should import client components from their own path, `@once-ui-system/core/components/Button`, so that it does not ship every component.

- `src/resources/app.ts`: product name, user and nav. The sidebar, breadcrumb and ⌘K palette all read it. Each nav href needs a page under `src/app/(app)/`; copy `home/page.tsx`.
- `src/resources/once-ui.config.ts`: brand, accent, neutral and `defaultTheme` (`theme` itself stays `"system"`, or the theme switch stops working).
- `src/components/AppShell.tsx`: the frame. Change it only to change the frame; it already covers the app-shell bundle's quality bar.

Then build each page from the bundle below that fits it.

## Writing a page or feature

Every file you read is sent again on every later turn, so read what you need in one step, then write.

1. Pick the bundle below closest to what you are building and read it, together with any project files you need (in a Next.js app at least `app/layout.tsx`, which mounts the providers), in a single step. Open those project files by path: listing their folder first costs a turn, and every turn re-sends the bundle. A bundle is complete: the rules, every component's props, types, gotchas, the quality bar and a gold example. Read one bundle, not two: a second one doubles what every later turn re-sends, and a component it adds is cheaper as its `ai/components/<Name>.json` slice. Then write the code.
2. Need a component the bundle does not list? Every bundle has the components in the `page.md` row; the Adds column names what each one carries on top. Read the `ai/components/<Name>.json` of anything else your page needs in that same step, not after the bundle.
3. Nothing fits? Read `ai/bundles/page.md` (the rules and the common components) with the `ai/components/<Name>.json` slices your page needs, in one step. `ai/catalog.json` names every component with its purpose.

Never open `ai/spec.json`: it is the full machine spec, for tooling.

<!-- tasks:start -->
| Bundle | For | Adds |
|---|---|---|
| `ai/bundles/marketing-hero.md` | Marketing hero: Headline with text effect, CTA pair, social proof logos, background effect | Background, RevealFx, LetterFx, LogoCloud, Line |
| `ai/bundles/pricing.md` | Pricing page: Three tiers, highlighted middle tier, feature comparison table, FAQ accordion | Background, MatrixFx, BlobFx, RevealFx, CountFx, SegmentedControl, Table, AccordionGroup |
| `ai/bundles/settings.md` | Settings page: Vertical section tabs, profile form, settings rows with one control each, grouped sub-settings, danger zone | Tabs, TabList, Tab, TabPanel, Form, Select, Setting, Tooltip, Switch, Slider, NumberInput, Checkbox, MediaUpload, Table, NavItem |
| `ai/bundles/dashboard.md` | Analytics dashboard: KPI stat cards, charts area, recent-activity list | Background, CountFx, StatusIndicator, Table, SegmentedControl, LineChart, BarChart, ChartHeader, RevealFx, Line, Drawer, NavItem |
| `ai/bundles/chat.md` | Chat UI: Message list with avatars, typing indicator, composer with send and attach, conversation list | ChatMessageList, ChatMessage, ChatComposer, TypingIndicator, ConversationItem, SplitView, EmojiPicker, Fade, Kbd, User, Line |
| `ai/bundles/auth.md` | Auth flow: Sign-up / login with social auth, email form, stacked dialog for OTP | OTPInput, Media, SmartLink, Line |
| `ai/bundles/roadmap.md` | Product roadmap: Kanban-style roadmap with status columns and task cards | Card, StatusIndicator, User, Scroller |
| `ai/bundles/list-page.md` | List / table page: A page of records: title with the primary action, a status filter, a searchable, sortable, paginated Table with status tags and row actions, and an empty state | SegmentedControl, Select, Table, Dropdown, Option, Map, MapMarkers, MapPin, MapPopup |
| `ai/bundles/editor.md` | Editor shell: A toolbar, a resizable two-pane split (layers and canvas) and a timeline spanning both — video editor, page builder, diff view | SplitView, Scrubber, ToggleButton, Media, MediaVideoPlayer |
| `ai/bundles/docs-page.md` | Docs or blog article: An MDX article: breadcrumb trail, title and summary, Markdown rendered through the /mdx component map, and an on-page heading nav | Breadcrumbs, HeadingNav, MdxHeading, Feedback, CodeBlock |
| `ai/bundles/app-shell.md` | App shell: Signed-in app frame shared by several routes: sidebar with nested nav groups and the current route highlighted, header with breadcrumb, account or workspace menu and command palette, phone drawer | Nav, NavGroup, NavItem, Drawer, Breadcrumbs, User, Dropdown, Option, Kbar, Kbd, Line, Table |
| `ai/bundles/page.md` | Any other page: The rules and the components nearly every page uses, with their types and gotchas. Read it with the `components/<Name>.json` slices your page adds, in one step | Column, Row, Grid, Heading, Text, Button, IconButton, Icon, Input, Textarea, Tag, Badge, Avatar, Dialog, Skeleton, VisuallyHidden; this bundle alone also has Switch, SegmentedControl, Select, Checkbox, Card |
<!-- tasks:end -->

Validate generated code: `npx once-ui-validate-ai-code path/to/file.tsx`. Without a bundle, app shells, sidebars and editors are in `ai/layouts.md`, and Pro blocks to compose from are listed in `ai/examples/blocks/manifest.json`.

## Phone apps

`@once-ui-system/native` has the same components and props for React Native, with its own harness for phone screens: `node_modules/@once-ui-system/native/AGENTS.md`. For an app on the web and on phones, build each from its own package's bundles and share the content and the theme options.

## Setup

`npx once-ui-init-agent` points a consumer app's AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md and Cursor rules here. Without `node_modules`, use https://docs.once-ui.com/ai/manifest.json (may not match your installed version exactly).

# Any other page The rules and the components nearly every page uses, with their types and gotchas. Read it with the `components/.json` slices your page adds, in one step This file is complete for this task: the rules (all of `rules.compact.md`), the props of every component below, their mixins and types, every gotcha for these components, the quality bar and a gold example. Write the page from it; reading the rules, catalog, gotchas, manifest or examples again only adds cost. Open `components/.json` only for a component not listed here, and then every one you need in a single step. ## Rules ### Layout | Write | Never write | |-------|-------------| | `` | `` | | `` | ``, or `` with no direction | | `fill` | `fillWidth fillHeight` | | `fit` | `fitWidth fitHeight` | | `center` | `horizontal="center" vertical="center"` | | `maxWidth="l"` | `fillWidth maxWidth="l"` | | `fillWidth` | `fillWidth minWidth={0}` | | `width={32} height={32}` (a number is the token: `32` = `"32"` = 2rem), `maxWidth="40rem"` | `maxWidth={40}` for 40rem (that was 2.x: `40` is now `"40"`, 2.5rem) | | `border` | `border="neutral-alpha-weak"` | | `` | a `` and a `` | - Units: a number is on the **token scale** on every size, spacing and offset prop: `16` = `"16"` = 1rem, scaled by `data-scaling` (`width={320}`, `padding={24}`, `top={8}`), in breakpoint objects too; a digit string is the spacing token (`"16"`); any CSS length string passes through (`"320px"` never scales, `"50%"`, `"100dvh"`). `Mask`/`Background` percentages are strings (`x="50%"`) - Control size for a whole app: `density: "compact" | "normal" | "spacious"` in the config `style` (`data-density`), not `size="s"` on every Button; it also picks scaling 95/100/105 unless `scaling` is set. Give `size` only where one control differs - `Flex` only when direction changes at breakpoints: `` - Subtree theme: `theme`, `themeBorder`, `themeSolid`, `themeSurface` on Flex/Row/Column/Grid and components built on them (`Background`, `Tag`, effects) — not raw `data-theme`/`data-border`/`data-solid`. `Button`/`IconButton` have no typed prop: keep `data-border="rounded"` - App theme in `once-ui.config` `style`: `defaultTheme: "light"` = starts light, visitor can switch (`theme: "light"` forces it and `setTheme` does nothing). Exact brand colours: `brandScale`/`neutralScale` `{ 100: "#…", …, 1200: "#…" }` (with or without a seed; per theme `{ light: {…}, dark: {…} }`), page/card colour: `pageBackground`/`surfaceBackground` (token or colour, or `{ light, dark }`), not overrides of semantic CSS variables - Page skeleton: `Column as="main" fillWidth horizontal="center"` → content `Column maxWidth="l"` → sections - Section gaps: `"104"` between sections, `"24"`–`"40"` inside. Never `"48"` between major sections. - Responsive: breakpoint props `xl l m s xs` — never media queries for layout ### Surfaces Static panel recipe (pricing tiers, stats, settings sections): ```tsx ``` - Bare `border` (and `borderTop`, `borderBottom`, …) = the default border. Name a colour only to deviate: `border="brand-alpha-medium"`. - `Card` = interactive only (`href` or `onClick`). Static panels = Column + surface recipe. - Colors: `{tone}-{weight}` or `{tone}-alpha-{weight}`. Never hex/rgb — inline SVG `fill`/`stroke` included: `currentColor` or `var(--brand-solid-strong)`. - `background` also: `surface | overlay | page | transparent` ### Typography - Hero: `display-strong-l` or `display-strong-xl` - Section titles: `display-strong-xs` or `display-strong-s` — not `heading-*` - Eyebrow: `` - Text on layout: `textVariant` + `onBackground` on Row/Column instead of nesting Text ### Decoration Absolute layers always: `position="absolute" top="0" left="0" fill pointerEvents="none"`, content `zIndex={1}`. - `zIndex` only inside that layer group (or on a sticky header over its pane). Never on a lone element, never a page-wide ladder. - Gradient `width`: quarter-percent (400 = 100%). Glows: 100–200. - Glow colors: `brand-alpha-medium`, not `brand-background-weak` - Ambient layers on full-bleed section wrapper, outside `maxWidth` column - Budget: one ambient layer per section; motion in hero + one CTA max ### Motion - Every `duration`, `delay` and interval is **milliseconds**: `delay={index * 100}` — `* 0.1` was 1.8.x; `CelebrationFx`/`WeatherFx` `duration={5000}`, not `{5}`. `RevealFx`/`ShineFx`/`CountFx` take `duration`, `TypeFx` `charDuration` (`speed` there was 2.x) - `speed` is only a multiplier, `1` the default, or `"slow"`/`"medium"`/`"fast"` (0.5/1/2): `MatrixFx`, `WeatherFx`, `ParticleFx`, `CelebrationFx`, `Effect`, `Scroller` `auto.speed`, `GlitchFx`, `LetterFx` - `RevealFx translateY`: a number is the token scale (`16` = 1rem); prefer `"8"`–`"16"` tokens - Viewport-reveal with `useInViewport` + latch into `RevealFx revealed`; `CountFx` driven by `value`, no trigger prop - Animate all siblings in a set or none — never one lone animated card ### Components | Need | Use | |------|-----| | Image | `Media` | | Link | `SmartLink` / `Button href` | | Status dot | `StatusIndicator` | | Loading | `Spinner` / `Skeleton` | | Scroll fade | `Fade` as edge strip, not wrapper | | Icons | `IconName` (the IconName type below) only | | Logos grid | `LogoCloud` with `columns` set | | Tabs | `Tabs` > `TabList` > `Tab`, `TabPanel` (`orientation="vertical"` for a settings nav) | | Mobile nav, side sheet | `Drawer`, not a hand-made overlay | | Page trail | `Breadcrumbs items={[...]}` | | Keyboard shortcut | `useHotkeys("mod+k", fn)` + `Kbd keys="mod+k" label="Search"` | | Screen-reader text, skip link | `VisuallyHidden` (skip link: ``) | | Native attributes | Every component also takes its element's own: `aria-*`, `id`, `role`, `onClick`; `type` on `Button`; `value`, `onChange`, `type` on `Input` | | MDX content | `mdxComponents` / `createMdxComponents` from `/mdx` | | Multi-part component | List prop (`items`, `columns`, `options`) for same-shaped data, else plain named parts (`SortableItem`, `StylePanelBrand`); never `Sortable.Item` | ### Imports Most things come from the package root. These do not — each component below says where it comes from when it is not the root: | Import | From | |--------|------| | charts, gauges, chart chrome | `@once-ui-system/core/data` | | `CodeBlock` | `@once-ui-system/core/code` (needs `prismjs`) | | `MediaUpload` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` (needs `compressorjs`) | | `Map`, `MapMarker(s)`, `MapPin`, `MapPopup`, `MapCircle` | `@once-ui-system/core/map` (needs `maplibre-gl`) | | `mdxComponents`, `createMdxComponents`, `Mdx*` elements | `@once-ui-system/core/mdx` (needs `prismjs`) | | `MediaAudioPlayer`, `MediaVideoPlayer`, `Scrubber`, `CompareImage` | `@once-ui-system/core/media` | | `EmojiPicker` | `@once-ui-system/core/emoji` | | `LayoutProvider` in a **Next.js** app; `createOgFetchRoute`, `createOgProxyRoute` | `@once-ui-system/core/next` | | `defineConfig`, `OnceUIConfig` in `once-ui.config` | `@once-ui-system/core/config` (also on the root) | | the effects: `RevealFx`, `CountFx`, `TypeFx`, `MatrixFx`, `Effect`, every `*Fx` | `@once-ui-system/fx` (a package: install it) | | `Banner`, `Book`, `LogoCloud`, `ScrollToTop`, `StylePanel`, `StyleOverlay` | `@once-ui-system/blocks` (a package: install it) | Naming one of these from the root does not resolve — except `defineConfig`, which is on both, and `LayoutProvider`, which resolves and then silently renders links and images as plain `` and `` in a Next.js app. `IconName` is a real union, so an unregistered icon name is a type error, not a blank space — take names (the IconName type below). Brand marks are not in the set: an app registers them by augmenting `IconLibraryOverrides`. ### Types — the common type errors Every type a prop names is defined in the slice's (or bundle's) `types`. - Responsive `xl`/`l`/`m`/`s`/`xs` props exist only on `Flex`, `Row`, `Column` and `Grid`. To change a `Button`, `Text` or anything else at a breakpoint, wrap it in one of those; `Text` and `Heading` take only `s={{ hide: true }}`. Leaves (`Button`, the fields and controls, `Text`, `Heading`, `Icon`, `Avatar`, `Kbd`…) take only margins, `flex`, `fillWidth`, `position` and offsets, `className` and `style`: padding, background, border, radius, sizes and anything else at a breakpoint go on a wrapper too. - `vertical`/`horizontal` take `start | center | end | between | around | even | stretch` — no `baseline`; for baseline-aligned text write `style={{ alignItems: "baseline" }}`. - Spacing (`gap`, `padding`, …) takes the SpacingToken values below: `"4"`, `"8"`, `"12"`, `"16"`, `"20"`, `"24"`, `"32"`, `"40"`… — there is no `"6"` or `"10"`. - `as` on `Flex`/`Row`/`Column`/`Grid` types the element's attributes and ref: ``, ``. `as="ul"`/`"ol"` drops bullets and indent, `as="button"` the button chrome; other components take no `as`. - `Row`, `Column` and `Grid` have no `span`: a child spanning grid columns uses `style={{ gridColumn: "span 2" }}`. - `variant` is appearance (Button: `primary | secondary | tertiary | ghost | link`), `tone` the palette (`brand | accent | neutral | info | success | warning | danger`) on Button, IconButton, Tag, Feedback, Toast and `addToast`: `

content.thinking: I've settled on a design: shared state in `lib/data.ts`, a wizard, a summary card, and a welcome page that reads the saved values from `sessionStorage`. Theme changes will apply live through `useTheme().setTheme`, and step 1 is pre-filled from the user data.
